section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion summarizes a single study examining the factor structure and psychometric properties of the Persian BAS-2 in an Iranian university sample, finding a one-factor structure and internal consistency for men and women. It reports small positive associations between BAS-2 and self-esteem/life satisfaction, a negative association between BAS-2 and BMI in women and positive associations in men, small positive associations with age, and small sex differences favoring men; limitations include use of a university sample, self-reported BMI, and absence of ethnicity data.
section_summary.evidence_source: Summary drawn from multiple sentences in the Discussion, including: 'The present study aimed to examine the factor structure and psychometric properties of the BAS-2 in Iran.'; 'Of note, the Persian BAS-2 was negatively associated with BMI in women. BMI and BMI2 were positively associated with body appreciation in men.'; and 'The present study has several limitations... Second, self-reported BMI was used.'

section_summary.extract_value: This discussion reports validation of the Persian BAS-2 in an Iranian university sample, finding a one-factor structure and good internal consistency. Correlational results showed a small negative association between BAS-2 and BMI in women (r = -0.24) and a small positive association in men (r = 0.12); limitations include the university-only sample, use of self-reported BMI, and lack of ethnicity data.
